$schema_note: Application-AUTHORED display names and consumer notices for the fifteen governed records in 07_CONCERNS. NOT an official KOREA GLOW source, and not a replacement for any source field: Concern_ID and Concern_Name are used verbatim and unchanged. This file only adds what the source has no column for — the name a shopper would recognise in her own language, and one line describing what she might notice.
governanceNote: Every notice is claimClass OBSERVATIONAL. A notice states only what a person might SEE or FEEL. It never names a cause, never says what skin is or needs, never recommends an action, ingredient or product, and never mentions treating, curing, preventing, reducing or improving anything. CON-004 (Acne), CON-005 (Redness) and CON-013 (Scalp Flakes) carry a source Boundary; the app's existing professional-consultation notice raises it, and these lines deliberately do not restate or soften it. Review status is Draft and nothing in code promotes it.
translationNote: en, ko and fr were written directly. th and lo are drafted from the vocabulary Lao and Thai skincare sellers actually use (ສິວ, ຜິວແຫ້ງ, ຮູຂຸມຂົນ, ຮັງແຄ …) rather than machine-translated from English — but they have NOT been read by a native speaker, and the app already labels both catalogs UNREVIEWED_DRAFT on screen. `laoReview: true` marks the entries where even the NAME is a phrase I constructed rather than a term I could attest in use; those are the ones to put in front of the Lao senior partner first. Every Lao and Thai sentence wants a native pass regardless.
